description: A knowledge graph cross-referencing real, publicly-listed FP&A/financial-modeling Excel template galleries against this toolkit's own module coverage -- nodes are sources and template categories, edges are 'cites' (source -> category) and 'covered_by' (category -> finmodel module) or 'gap' (category -> null, with a reason). Built as a targeted companion to finmodel.catalog (which does the same cross-reference against CFI/BIWS/Macabacus specifically) -- this graph covers the broader FP&A-software-vendor template landscape instead.

categories.name: Sales quota & rep-capacity planning
categories.reason: real and distinct, but sales-ops-specific rather than general FP&A; a real future extension of finmodel.cohort_analysis's ramping-productivity-curve mechanics.

categories.name: WIP / percentage-of-completion contract accounting
categories.reason: a real, standard ASC 606 revenue-recognition method, but vertical-specific (construction/long-term-contract industries) rather than general-purpose.

categories.name: Annual Operating Plan (AOP)
categories.reason: an orchestration of already-built pieces (headcount, opex budget, revenue plan, capex) into one process artifact, not a distinct calculation.

categories.name: Month-end close checklist / financial close workflow
categories.reason: a process/workflow tracker, not a financial calculation.

categories.name: Trial-balance-to-financial-statements automation
categories.reason: ERP/bookkeeping-integration territory, outside this toolkit's corporate-finance/FP&A modeling scope.

categories.name: Generic what-if / scenario data table
categories.reason: the 2-axis sensitivity-table pattern used across every DCF-based check this toolkit already runs.

categories.name: Cost-benefit analysis
categories.reason: a thin NPV-of-benefits-less-costs wrapper around an existing primitive; no distinct new formula to add.

categories.name: Balance sheet / income statement / cash flow statement templates
Personal-finance calculators (mortgage payoff, retirement, personal budget)
categories.reason: consumer/personal-finance tooling, outside this toolkit's corporate-finance and FP&A scope.
